text: Two variables of primitive type can be aliases for the same storage.
explanation: Assigning one primitive to another copies the value, so afterwards the two are independent — this is why local primitives are automatically safe across threads, as Chapter 31 notes. Aliasing requires a reference, which is why it appears exactly when objects do. The one apparent exception, an array element passed around, is not one: what is shared is the array, and the element is reached through it.
